sections.title: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents
sections.abstract: A closed-loop framework connecting agentic data production, model training, and model–harness co-evolution for long-horizon mobile planning.
sections.claimed_contribution: AI for Data, AI for Training, and execution-evidence-driven model–harness co-evolution; the authors report best overall performance among evaluated systems on MobilePA-Bench.
sections.caveat: New preprint; independent replication and benchmark comparability are not yet available.

sections.title: Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data
sections.abstract: Jointly trains a generator and learner from random initialization, with reinforcement learning generating computable sequences at the learner’s capability frontier.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report predictable zero-shot-loss scaling with self-play compute, in-context learning, and discovery of recognizable mathematical sequences.
sections.caveat: Initial proof of concept; transfer from synthetic computable sequences to broad real-world pretraining remains unresolved.

sections.title: ExplorationBench: Measuring AI Systems' Exploration in Verifiable Alien Worlds
sections.abstract: Evaluates discovery and application of unfamiliar rules in executable alien worlds designed to defeat simple pretraining recall.
sections.claimed_contribution: AlienCode and AlienLogic provide 140 tasks in total; the authors report substantial trajectory variance and possible regressions during continued exploration.
sections.caveat: Deliberately designed sandboxes may not predict open-world scientific discovery.

sections.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance
sections.abstract: Combines algebraic sparsification and hyperbolic structural guidance to reduce exploration and compounding biases in sparse-reward long-horizon reasoning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Symbolic Closure Analysis and SAGE; they report gains across 12 benchmarks and 7 model families, including an up-to-eight-fold improvement on Andrews–Curtis.
sections.caveat: Transfer of the structural priors to less formal reasoning tasks needs independent testing.

sections.title: ActGov: Governing LLM Agent Actions via Policy-Constrained Validation
sections.abstract: Validates every proposed tool action against task-scoped authorization and policies synthesized from specifications, benign tasks, and failure traces.
sections.claimed_contribution: ActGov-Policy and ActGov-Runtime use SMT checking and per-action enforcement; the authors report reduced indirect prompt-injection success while preserving utility.
sections.caveat: Deployment against evolving tool ecosystems and adaptive attackers remains open.

sections.title: BabelArena: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: Extends agent evaluation to 23 languages using structure-preserving translation and verification over 16,146 instances derived from 702 tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report low-resource-language tool/control-flow failures and up to roughly twice the English input-token use without proportional interaction-length gains.
sections.caveat: Translation and benchmark construction choices can affect cross-language comparisons.
